sn8.1:1.2: This chapter features the poetry of Vaṅgīsa, the finest poet of the Saṅgha, providing a prose setting for his Theragāthā verses at [thag21.1](). There are notable differences between the two versions. In several passages, including this one, he reflects on the struggles he faced in his path, showing a high degree of self-awareness and persistence.
sn8.1:1.4: Period art depicts women as bare-breasted and draped in elaborate jewelry.
sn8.1:1.5: “Dissatisfaction” (_anabhirati_) with his life of seclusion and celibacy.
sn8.1:3.1: There is some confusion regarding the Pali _ugga_ (“warrior chief”). Pali commentaries and Sanskrit sources (Manu 10.9) speak of a caste called _ugga_ (Sanskrit _ugra_), born of a _khattiya_ father and a _sudda_ mother. They were reviled as cruel, and their duty was to catch snakes and other underground vermin (Manu 10.49). This is not the aristocratic warriors referred to here. The distinction is noted in Medhātithi’s commentary to Manu 4.212, who says the Vedic _ugra_ was a key figure in the king’s alliance, which is supported by the use at [dn3:2.7.2]().
